llm.summary: This VMware-wide policy/audit skill is not malicious, but it needs Review because its central enforcement layer documents a global bypass and fail-open policy behavior.

dimensions.detail: The skill reads environment state for agent detection and policy switches. Agent detection is described as read-only and not logging token values, but VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED is an overbroad escape hatch for policy checks.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation is via uv as a Python package and dependency of other VMware skills. The artifact is documentation-only, but installing it brings in a CLI and policy/audit library used across the VMware skill family.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Auto-loading for any VMware skill is broad, but it is disclosed and aligned with the package's role as an infrastructure dependency. It exposes no MCP tools itself.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: It persistently records broad operational metadata in a local SQLite audit database under ~/.vmware, including parameters, results, user, agent, workflow, risk level, and denied/bypassed actions. This is purpose-aligned but sensitive and requires careful local protection.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The purpose is coherent: audit logging, policy enforcement, sanitization, and read-only gating for VMware skills. The concern is that the same central policy layer can allow all operations when rules are absent or PyYAML is missing, and can be bypassed with VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED=1.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with a VMware-wide local audit and policy layer. Before using it in production, set explicit rules, protect ~/.vmware with restrictive permissions, treat audit exports as sensitive, avoid using VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED except for tightly controlled break-glass cases, and verify PyYAML is installed so policy checks are actually active.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] expected: The broad activation is expected for a shared VMware policy dependency and is disclosed, so this is not independently suspicious.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The global VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED bypass is artifact-backed and materially weakens a policy-enforcement component because operations proceed while checks are disabled.
[SQP-2] expected: Credential-bearing local file outputs are discussed as write tools to be withheld by the read-only gate; the concern is partly mitigated because the artifact explicitly classifies them as write side effects.
[SQP-2] expected: Audit export to stdout/files is expected for an audit CLI, but the logs contain operational metadata and should be treated as confidential.
[SQP-2] expected: Persistent local audit and policy files are expected for this purpose and are disclosed, with chmod guidance, though operators should understand that missing rules mean allow-all.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The documented PyYAML failure mode silently allows all operations, which is a material fail-open behavior for a policy enforcement layer.
